title: Labs choose what to publish: α 1, 0.8, 0.2 × 10 runs, $0.15 a lab (Nov 8)

design.question: For the same agents, checker and money, does a community prove more targets when value flows back (OSO) than when results are only shared, or kept private until a target is proved?
design.compare: Labs choose, α 1, Labs choose, α 0.8, Labs choose, α 0.2
design.fixed: the same 4 agents (the single agent: the first, with all the money), $0.60 in all, Lean checks every proof
design.measure: the share of lemmas published at once (of those with a PUBLISH line), α 0.2 against α 1; targets proved beside it

answer: Lemmas published at once: Labs choose, α 1 99% (95% range 98% to 100%); Labs choose, α 0.8 99% (95% range 97% to 100%); Labs choose, α 0.2 100% (95% range 99% to 100%). α 0.2 minus α 1: 1% (95% range -1% to 2%).

caveats: Labs could not stop early: each worked until its money or the rounds ran out, so setups are compared at the same money spent.

Rewards differ from the current simulation model: the knowledge reward is measured by proof size (log2(1 + symbols/40), at most 4), a stand-in for the simulation's log2(1/p) per new bit; the simulation's prediction for sharing comes from its own fields, not from this problem set with this reward; a lab could pad its proofs, so sizes are checked against runs without the reward; value flowing back is split by the money spent proving each parent, not by the work a parent saves (1/p) as in the simulation.
Table values are mean ± standard deviation over runs. Above: means with 95% ranges (Student t), and differences between setups with their 95% ranges; runs are not paired.
